public_rationale: The available evidence does not establish that every AI app sells below its delivery cost. Bessemer reported positive average gross margins in a selected startup cohort, which is meaningful counterevidence to the blanket assertion. But its figures do not match a specified app, quarter and subsidy definition. The claim also supplies no accounting basis, which independently prevents a supported or contradicted money verdict under these rules. Investor funding or company-wide losses would not fill those gaps.
limitations: Gross margins do not establish coverage of research, marketing and other operating expenses.
Positive downstream margins do not rule out subsidies in upstream services.
The target quarter is an interpretation of an undated ongoing state.

from_speaker: Every single AI app is subsidized
our_interpretation: The ordinary testable reading is that every commercial generative-AI application charges less than the cost of delivering its service and therefore requires subsidy.
The surrounding discussion concerns generative-AI applications. I do not extend the claim to every historical use of machine learning.
Fake price and none of this is real are treated as rhetoric accompanying the subsidy claim, not separate accounting measures.
For this ongoing financial state, I use July through September 2025, the latest completed calendar quarter ordinarily reportable before the December 29 post.
The wording supplies no accounting basis or cited financial source. The contract therefore retains unknown accounting_basis, which prevents a supported or contradicted money verdict.
App-level delivery economics, company-wide net losses, and subsidies embedded in upstream model prices are separate questions.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable app-level records establish that every application in the defined population earned less from customers than its delivery costs during the target period and required external subsidy.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one in-scope application demonstrably covered its delivery costs without subsidy during the target period, using a defined and comparable accounting basis.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A defined cost and accounting basis, followed by matched third-quarter 2025 app-level revenue, delivery-cost and subsidy records.
